chapters.1.summary: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, the LORD stirs the king’s spirit. Cyrus sends a written order through his kingdom. He says the God of heaven has told him to build a house in Jerusalem. Any of God’s people may go up and build it. Their neighbors are to help with silver, gold, goods, and animals. Family heads, priests, and Levites prepare to go. Cyrus brings out the temple vessels that Nebuchadnezzar took. They are counted out to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.
chapters.1.lds: Come, Follow Me studies how people outside the community can help God’s work. Who is invited to go up in verse 3?
chapters.2.summary: This chapter lists the people who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and Jeshua. Families are counted by ancestor and by home town. Priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants follow. Some families cannot prove that they belong to Israel. Some priests cannot find their family records. The governor bars them from the holy food until a priest can decide. The whole company numbers 42,360, with servants and singers besides. Family heads give gold, silver, and priestly garments for the work.
chapters.2.lds: The Seminary introduction describes the families returning from exile, or forced life abroad. What do their gifts help rebuild?
chapters.3.summary: In the seventh month the people gather in Jerusalem as one. Jeshua and Zerubbabel build the altar on its old base. They fear the neighboring peoples and offer sacrifices morning and evening. They keep the Feast of Booths before any foundation is laid. They pay masons and carpenters and order cedar from Lebanon. In the second year the builders lay the temple’s foundation. Priests blow trumpets, and Levites sing that the LORD is good. Old men who saw the first house weep while others shout for joy.
chapters.3.lds: Come, Follow Me considers the joy and grief accompanying temple rebuilding. Who weeps in verse 12, and why?
chapters.4.summary: Neighbors of Judah and Benjamin offer to help build the temple. Zerubbabel and the leaders refuse. The neighbors then discourage the builders and hire advisers against them. This continues from the reign of Cyrus to that of Darius. Later, officials write to King Artaxerxes about Jerusalem’s walls. They call it a rebellious city that will stop paying taxes. The king searches the records and orders the building to stop. Work on God’s house ceases until the second year of Darius.
chapters.4.lds: Come, Follow Me studies responses to opposition. What does the king order in verse 21, and what does he leave open?
chapters.5.summary: The prophets Haggai and Zechariah speak to the Jews in God’s name. Zerubbabel and Jeshua begin again to build the house. Tattenai, the governor west of the River, asks who authorized them. He takes down the builders’ names. The work continues while he writes to King Darius. His letter reports the elders’ answer in full. They say Cyrus ordered the house rebuilt and returned its vessels. Tattenai asks the king to search the royal archives.
chapters.5.lds: Come, Follow Me asks how the people continue God’s work despite opposition. How do the elders identify themselves in verse 11?
chapters.6.summary: Darius orders a search of the archives. A scroll is found in the fortress of Achmetha in Media. It records Cyrus’s decree, with the temple’s size and the crown’s payment. Darius tells Tattenai to leave the work alone. He orders the costs paid from the region’s taxes. He supplies animals, wheat, salt, wine, and oil for the offerings. The elders finish the house in the sixth year of Darius. They dedicate it with joy and keep the Passover.
chapters.6.lds: Come, Follow Me studies the temple's opening and the people's joy. Where is the scroll found in verse 2?
chapters.7.summary: Years later Ezra comes up from Babylon. He is a priest of Aaron’s line and a scribe skilled in Moses’s law. King Artaxerxes grants all he asks. The journey takes about four months. The king’s letter lets any Israelite go with him. It sends silver and gold for offerings and frees temple workers from tax. It tells Ezra to appoint judges and teach God’s laws. Ezra blesses the LORD, who put this in the king’s heart.
chapters.7.lds: The Church lesson joins scripture study with practice and teaching. What three things had Ezra set his heart to do (verse 10)?
chapters.8.summary: Ezra lists the family heads who travel with him. At the river Ahava he finds no Levites in the camp. He sends for some, and Levites and temple servants join. He calls a fast and asks God for a safe road. He is ashamed to ask the king for soldiers. He weighs the silver, gold, and vessels into the hands of twelve priests. They reach Jerusalem safely. On the fourth day everything is weighed again and written down.
chapters.8.lds: The Seminary lesson studies fasting, prayer, and trust before the journey. What must the priests do with the gifts in verse 29?
chapters.9.summary: Leaders tell Ezra that the people have married among the neighboring peoples. Priests, Levites, and officials are among them. Ezra tears his clothes and sits appalled until the evening offering. Then he kneels and prays. He says the people’s guilt has grown up to the heavens. God has given them a little relief and a foothold in his holy place. They are still servants under Persia’s kings. He asks how they can break the commandments again.
chapters.9.lds: The Seminary lesson connects these marriages with worship of other gods. Ezra gives no personal testimony from the wives. How does Ezra describe his people’s condition in verse 9?
chapters.10.summary: While Ezra prays and weeps, a large crowd gathers and weeps with him. Shecaniah proposes a covenant to send away the foreign wives and their children. Ezra makes the leaders swear to it. All the men are called to Jerusalem within three days. They sit in the open square, trembling in heavy rain. Family heads are chosen to examine each case. The work takes three months. The book ends with a list of the men, and some had children.
chapters.10.lds: The Seminary lesson studies confession and repentance. What voices are missing from the account of separated families?
